A1.justification: Both complete 38-page PDFs describe TimeRCD and include Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original TimeRCD benchmark results, contextual-anomaly experiments, sensitivity analyses, and data/model ablations in Section 3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1 benchmark comparisons and Appendix E’s contextual, scaling, and head-ablation experiments.

M1.justification: TimeRCD retains the same tokenization, Transformer backbone, anomaly/reconstruction heads, training objectives, inference procedure, and synthetic-data generation method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 replaces WADI with SMAP, correcting its dataset list: v1 already includes SMAP in Table 8 and the corresponding result tables. The same 14 benchmark datasets, synthetic test scenarios, and pre-training data coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The zero-shot and full-shot comparator sets in Table 1 are identical. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the contextual experiments and data/head ablations in Appendix E.

E3.justification: The evaluation protocol, four metrics, baseline window sizes, training settings, dataset-specific context selections, and ablation/scaling budgets match throughout Section 3 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: The contextual-versus-point-anomaly tests, window-size sensitivity analysis, pre-training data comparisons, scaling studies, and anomaly/reconstruction-head ablations are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Seed information and uncertainty displays are unchanged, including Table 3’s optional generator-seed control. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All matched numerical scores, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged. This includes the main results in Tables 1–2 and the extended experimental results in Tables 9–13 and Appendix E’s figures.

T1.justification: The task definition, model equations, ODE-to-ARX construction, and Appendix C’s formal definitions of trends, seasonality, and anomaly types are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about RCD, fully synthetic pre-training, and zero-shot anomaly-detection performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of context length, injection trade-offs, data scaling, and reconstruction-head necessity are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same limitation and future direction concerning the standard Transformer backbone.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code-availability footnote identifying the Time-RCD GitHub repository. This provides new access information; existing implementation and training details remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish repository accessibility or completeness.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix B are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to reconstruction-based TSAD, contrastive methods, and synthetic-data pre-training.

P1.justification: v3 removes affiliation lines, corrects an author email, adds the code footnote, and corrects WADI to SMAP in Appendix D.1. The substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened author block and added footnote produce limited reflow on pages 1–4, including slight repositioning of Figures 2–3. No figures or tables are added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reproducibility documentation by adding a code-access reference and improves internal consistency by correcting D.1’s WADI/SMAP mismatch with the existing tables. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific evidence is unchanged, and repository usability cannot be established from the PDFs.
